subject: TTFT & streaming SLO follow-up / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 22:05:00 +0000
Subject: TTFT & streaming SLO follow-up / next steps

Thanks again for the call today, Alex — good to sync. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we’re aligned on performance requirements and what Redwood will surface in the POC.

Recap of FF requirements (from your side):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): target <= 150 ms p95 for interactive flows (checkout assistant & product search assistant).
- Streaming: partial output needed for streaming UI. Prefer SSE in browser but OK with WebSocket if it improves reliability.
- Chunk cadence: UX needs a chunk every ~100–250 ms for short responses (<= 8 tokens) and burst cadence for long responses; best-effort per-token streaming when possible.
- Throughput/concurrency: baseline 200 concurrent active users with peak ~500 RPS; steady-state throughput for embedding/rerank separate.
- Fallbacks: acceptable to degrade to short-first-token + batch completion if concurrency spikes, but TTFT SLO should be met for the top-tier routes.

What we’ll deliver for the POC:
1) Perf harness run against a representative endpoint (SSE + WebSocket) with traffic shape you shared.
2) Baseline TTFT numbers (p50/p95/p99) and chunk cadence distribution.
3) Suggested config: batching, KV caching, model variant recommendation and quantization tradeoffs to meet SLOs.

Action items / next steps:
- Marissa (me): schedule technical sync + share perf harness link and initial SLO matrix (attached).
- Dev (engineering): confirm required sample payloads and chunking semantics we should simulate.
- Alex: confirm the busiest route(s) and whether the 150 ms p95 applies to all routes or only the checkout assistant.

If that matches your recollection I’ll schedule a 30–45m tech call early this week to run through the harness and get Dev’s questions answered.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Rivera <alex@fastcommerce.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 01:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLO follow-up / next steps

Thanks Marissa — that all looks right. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 150 ms p95 is our bar for the checkout assistant route only. Product search can tolerate up to 250 ms p95.
- For streaming we prefer SSE in the browser for quick integration, but our mobile apps use WebSocket. We want both covered in the POC.
- Chunk cadence: for checkout we need very low latency for short replies (often 2–6 tokens). 100 ms cadence is ideal; 250 ms is the absolute max before UX degrades.

Happy to take the tech call — afternoons PST are best. Also please add the following to the perf runs: TLS enabled, and simulate cold-starts (no cache) and warm runs.

Appreciate you and the team moving quickly on this — looking forward to the data.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of AI, FastCommerce
alex@fastcommerce.com | (212) 555-0123

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 03:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLO follow-up / next steps

Thanks — adding a couple technical notes and questions before the POC run:

Notes:
- SSE vs WebSocket: SSE is simpler for browser clients and supports automatic reconnect semantics; WebSocket gives lower overhead for two-way messages and may help reduce TTFT slightly in some network conditions. We'll run both in the harness.
- TTFT measurement: we’ll report TTFT as time from request wire-to-wire to the first byte of model-generated token (including TLS handshake where applicable). We'll provide p50/p95/p99 and a distribution of chunk intervals.
- Cadence emulation: we can emulate per-token cadence (worst-case), and a batched-chunk cadence (e.g., 50–100 ms groups). Need guidance on payload encoding (JSON lines vs. SSE event types).

Questions for Alex / FF team:
1) For checkout assistant short replies, are you expecting the assistant to stream partial tokens (char/byte-level) or token-level frames? Token-level streaming is what our runtime natively supports.
2) Do you have a sample 0/1/2-turn prompt bundle we should use for latency-sensitive routes? If not, we'll use the example prompts you previously shared (thanks).

Proposed test matrix (we'll run this for both SSE and WebSocket):
- Cold start, small prompt (2–6 tokens output), 100 RPS sustained, 200 concurrency ramp -> measure TTFT distribution.
- Warm cache, larger prompt (50–200 tokens), 50 RPS, burst to 500 RPS -> measure chunk cadence, end-to-end latency.
- TLS + proxy hop (to simulate mobile)

I’ll prepare a run and attach the first harness CSV. Marissa — can you get us the sample prompts and confirm the target routes?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.com
